title: World Cup 2022 agent — monitoring
description: Online evaluation of the WC2022 routing agent: user feedback, LLM-as-judge relevance, cost, latency and tool routing.

panels.title: Feedback rate
panels.description: Answers per bucket split by the latest user thumb. A changed thumb inserts a new row, so only the most recent one per conversation counts.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(c.timestamp, $__interval, 0) AS time,
  SUM(CASE WHEN uf.score > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS thumbs_up,
  SUM(CASE WHEN uf.score < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS thumbs_down,
  SUM(CASE WHEN uf.conversation_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_feedback
FROM monitoring.conversations c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (conversation_id) conversation_id, score
  FROM monitoring.feedback
  WHERE source = 'user'
  ORDER BY conversation_id, timestamp DESC, id DESC
) uf ON uf.conversation_id = c.id
WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Response time
panels.description: Whole-loop latency, including tool calls. p95 is the one that matters — mixed-routing turns are much slower than SQL-only ones.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(c.timestamp, $__interval, NULL) AS time,
  AVG(c.response_time) AS avg_seconds,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY c.response_time) AS p95_seconds
FROM monitoring.conversations c
WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Cost — agent vs judge
panels.description: Judging every answer is a second LLM call, so it gets its own series.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(c.timestamp, $__interval, 0) AS time,
  SUM(c.cost) AS agent_cost,
  COALESCE(SUM(jf.cost), 0) AS judge_cost
FROM monitoring.conversations c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT conversation_id, SUM(cost) AS cost
  FROM monitoring.feedback
  WHERE source = 'judge'
  GROUP BY conversation_id
) jf ON jf.conversation_id = c.id
WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Tokens
panels.description: Prompt tokens dominate: the instructions are long and every tool result is echoed back into the next request.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroup(c.timestamp, $__interval, NULL) AS time,
  AVG(c.prompt_tokens) AS avg_prompt_tokens,
  AVG(c.completion_tokens) AS avg_completion_tokens,
  AVG(c.total_tokens) AS avg_total_tokens
FROM monitoring.conversations c
WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT
  f.relevance,
  COUNT(*) AS count
FROM monitoring.feedback f
WHERE f.source = 'judge'
  AND f.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY f.relevance
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Tool routing
panels.description: Which knowledge-base half each question reached: sql-only, prose-only, mixed, or none (answered or declined without tools).

targets.rawSql:
WITH tools AS (
  SELECT c.id,
         COALESCE(bool_or(e.call->>'name' = 'execute_sql'), false) AS used_sql,
         COALESCE(bool_or(e.call->>'name' IN ('search_prose', 'read_section')), false) AS used_prose
  FROM monitoring.conversations c
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(c.tool_calls) AS e(call) ON TRUE
  WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY c.id
),
paths AS (
  SELECT id,
         CASE WHEN used_sql AND used_prose THEN 'mixed'
              WHEN used_sql               THEN 'sql-only'
              WHEN used_prose             THEN 'prose-only'
              ELSE 'none' END AS tool_path
  FROM tools
)
SELECT tool_path, COUNT(*) AS conversations
FROM paths
GROUP BY tool_path
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Tool calls by tool
panels.description: Individual tool calls, so repeated SQL attempts show up.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  e.call->>'name' AS tool,
  COUNT(*) AS calls
FROM monitoring.conversations c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(c.tool_calls) AS e(call)
WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Feedback by tool path
panels.description: User thumbs and judge verdicts per routing path — where the agent is doing well and where it isn't.

targets.rawSql:
WITH tools AS (
  SELECT c.id,
         COALESCE(bool_or(e.call->>'name' = 'execute_sql'), false) AS used_sql,
         COALESCE(bool_or(e.call->>'name' IN ('search_prose', 'read_section')), false) AS used_prose
  FROM monitoring.conversations c
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(c.tool_calls) AS e(call) ON TRUE
  WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
  GROUP BY c.id
),
paths AS (
  SELECT id,
         CASE WHEN used_sql AND used_prose THEN 'mixed'
              WHEN used_sql               THEN 'sql-only'
              WHEN used_prose             THEN 'prose-only'
              ELSE 'none' END AS tool_path
  FROM tools
),
latest_user AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (f.conversation_id) f.conversation_id, f.score
  FROM monitoring.feedback f
  WHERE f.source = 'user'
  ORDER BY f.conversation_id, f.timestamp DESC, f.id DESC
),
latest_judge AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (f.conversation_id) f.conversation_id, f.relevance
  FROM monitoring.feedback f
  WHERE f.source = 'judge'
  ORDER BY f.conversation_id, f.timestamp DESC, f.id DESC
)
SELECT
  p.tool_path,
  SUM(CASE WHEN u.score > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS thumbs_up,
  SUM(CASE WHEN u.score < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS thumbs_down,
  SUM(CASE WHEN j.relevance = 'RELEVANT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS judge_relevant,
  SUM(CASE WHEN j.relevance = 'PARTLY_RELEVANT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS judge_partly,
  SUM(CASE WHEN j.relevance = 'NON_RELEVANT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS judge_non_relevant
FROM paths p
LEFT JOIN latest_user u ON u.conversation_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN latest_judge j ON j.conversation_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.tool_path
ORDER BY p.tool_path

panels.title: Recent conversations
panels.description: Latest turns with both scores side by side. Questions prefixed [seed] are fabricated by monitoring.seed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  c.timestamp AS time,
  c.question,
  LEFT(c.answer, 240) AS answer,
  j.relevance AS judge,
  u.score AS thumb,
  c.response_time,
  c.cost
FROM monitoring.conversations c
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT f.relevance FROM monitoring.feedback f
  WHERE f.conversation_id = c.id AND f.source = 'judge'
  ORDER BY f.timestamp DESC, f.id DESC LIMIT 1
) j ON TRUE
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT f.score FROM monitoring.feedback f
  WHERE f.conversation_id = c.id AND f.source = 'user'
  ORDER BY f.timestamp DESC, f.id DESC LIMIT 1
) u ON TRUE
WHERE c.timestamp BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
ORDER BY c.timestamp DESC
LIMIT 10
